title: Put Boxes Into the Warehouse II
summary: Given two arrays, boxes and warehouse, representing the heights of boxes and rooms in a warehouse, respectively, you must determine the maximum number of boxes that can be placed in the warehouse.
statement: Given two arrays, boxes and warehouse, representing the heights of boxes and rooms in a warehouse, respectively, you must determine the maximum number of boxes that can be placed in the warehouse. Boxes cannot be stacked, but their order can be rearranged, and they can be inserted from either end. If a room's height is less than a box's height, no boxes can be placed beyond that room. You can push boxes into the warehouse from either the left or the right.
constraints: Boxes may enter from either end and cannot pass through a lower room on that route.
Rearrange boxes and place at most one per room to maximize the count.
hints: A room’s left-entry capacity is the minimum height from the left through that room; its right-entry capacity is the analogous suffix minimum.
Take the larger of those two capacities because the box may use either entrance.
Sort capacities and boxes, then match the shortest remaining box to each room from smallest capacity upward.
Greedy matching preserves taller boxes and larger rooms for later, maximizing cardinality.
editorial: Greedy matching preserves taller boxes and larger rooms for later, maximizing cardinality.

tests.explanation: Using both entrances allows four boxes to occupy all rooms.
The central height-one bottleneck and entrance limits allow three boxes.
